message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of the key traffic laws and regulations that apply in Texas. (For the most up‑to‑date details, always check the Texas Department of Transportation or the Texas Transportation Code.) | Topic | What you need to know | |-------|-----------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • 55 mph on rural interstates
• 45 mph on urban interstates
• 35 mph on rural highways (unless posted otherwise)
• 25 mph on residential streets (unless posted otherwise) | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system). | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers and drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles on the right have priority unless signs indicate otherwise. | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 20 mph during school‑zone hours (unless posted otherwise). | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green light = go; yellow light = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop before proceeding. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals; check mirrors and blind spots.
• Do not pass on the left unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a stop sign, crosswalk, or intersection.
• No parking in handicap spaces unless you have a valid permit. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must display current registration stickers.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is unsafe or has been abandoned. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds have specific helmet and lighting requirements. | ### Quick Reference - **Speed limit signs**: Always obey posted limits; they can differ from the default values above. - **Seat‑belt law**: Failure to buckle can result in a fine and points on your license. - **Cell‑phone law**: Using a handheld device while driving can lead to a fine and points. - **DUI penalties**: First offense can carry fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. --- #### Want More Detail? If you’re looking for the exact statutory language or want to see how these rules apply in a specific situation (e.g., “What happens if I’m pulled over for speeding in a school zone?”), let me know and I can pull up the relevant sections of the Texas Transportation Code or provide a more tailored explanation.
